# REGIME READ — 2026-09-17

**[FULL READ — WebSearch available, fourth consecutive full run. The option chain fetched, so Layer 2 uses a quoted implied volatility.]** **The FOMC resolved, and it resolved HAWKISH: a 25bp hike, a 12–0 vote, and a dot plot showing 16 of 18 participants expecting another increase this year.** **One bearish trigger FIRED (the 10-year closed above 5.00%). One bullish trigger was DECIDED AGAINST (the dovish-FOMC surprise did not arrive). And the oil shock that has driven two lenses to the floor for a week began unwinding — Brent −6.04% on a credible pipeline-restart report.** **Total score improves for the first time in this series, from −9 to −7. The window ahead is CLEAN of scheduled macro events for the first time in three weeks. Quad-witching is tomorrow.**

## Changes Since Previous Read
- **Stage: 3 (Neutral/choppy) → 3 (Neutral/choppy)** — unchanged for a sixteenth consecutive read. **VIX sits inside the 15–22 band on both available measures: 15.99 on this morning's quote and 17.71 on the 2026-09-16 settle.** **The classification is robust to that ambiguity for once, which is more than can be said for the last three reads.**
- **Total score: −9 → −7 (delta +2).** **Two lenses upgraded — Cross-asset (−2 → −1) and Geopolitical (−2 → −1), both on the same underlying fact: the Saudi supply disruption is being repaired and oil is coming off.** **First improvement in this series. Composition: 0 bullish, 5 bearish, 2 neutral — eighth consecutive read with no bullish lens.**
- **Triggers from previous read:**
  - *Bearish — the 10-year yield CLOSING above 5.00%:* **FIRED.** **It missed by four tenths of a basis point yesterday and it fired today.** **The engine records 5.006% (+0.20%) for 2026-09-16.** **CNBC reports the benchmark "up 2 basis points at 5.016%" after the decision and Chair Warsh's press conference** ([CNBC, Sep 16](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/09/16/treasury-yield-bond-market-fed-decision.html)). **The two sources differ by one basis point; both are above 5.00%, so the trigger fires on either. This is the first 10-year close above 5% in this series and the highest since 2007.**
  - *Bullish — FOMC dovish surprise:* **DID NOT FIRE. RESOLVED HAWKISH, and decisively.** **The FOMC voted 12–0 to raise the target range 25bp to 3.75%–4.00% — the first increase since 2023** ([CNBC](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/09/16/fed-rate-decision-september-2026.html), [investinglive](https://investinglive.com/central-banks/fomc-rate-decision-fed-hikes-for-the-first-time-in-three-years/)). **The dot plot put the 2026 rate at 4.1%–4.4%, with 16 of 18 participants expecting at least one more hike this year and four seeing two more** ([Seeking Alpha](https://seekingalpha.com/article/4947278-feds-interest-rate-decision-september-16-2026)). **Yesterday I argued the surprise was two-sided — that dots BELOW the futures path (~4.2% for December) would be a dovish surprise delivered by a hawkish action. That tail existed and it did not pay. The dots came in at or above the market, not below it.**
  - *Bearish — Brent above $105 on two consecutive verified closes:* **FIRED last read; now REVERSING, not yet cleared.** **Brent $99.44, −6.04% (engine, 2026-09-17 live).** See the Data-integrity footnote — the level is disputed, the direction is not.
  - *Bearish — TQQQ closes below the 4-week low $67.34:* **DID NOT FIRE.** **TQQQ closed $67.93 (+0.04%) on 2026-09-16 — it held the line on the day the Fed hiked.** **Note carefully: the 4-week low has since rolled DOWN to $66.55 on a window roll, so the apparent margin widened from 0.83% to 2.07% while price moved three cents. See Finding 10.**
  - *Bearish — VIX above 20:* **ARMED and moved further away.** **VIX 15.99 this morning (−9.71% from a 09-16 settle of 17.71).** Needs **+25.08%** from the morning quote, or **+12.93%** from the settle.
  - *Bearish — VXN > 25:* **ARMED, barely moved.** **VXN 22.44, +0.81% (2026-09-16).** Needs **+11.41%** (was +12.31%).
  - *Bearish — NDX < 28,400:* **ARMED, fractionally further away.** NDX **28,945.06 (+0.02%)** needs **−1.88%**.
  - *Bearish — HY OAS through 3.25% WITH IG above 0.90%:* **ARMED.** **HY OAS 2.76% (+5bp from 2.71%), IG OAS 0.80% (unchanged)**, both **2026-09-15** (FRED). Needs **+49bp** on HY. **Credit widened again by a handful of basis points and remains extraordinarily tight.**
  - *Bullish — TQQQ reclaims the 50DMA and holds two sessions:* **ARMED, and the small improvement is not price.** Spot **$67.93** vs 50DMA **$70.72** — **−3.94%**, against −4.10% last read. **The 50DMA fell $0.08 and spot rose $0.03; the moving average did most of the closing.**
  - *Bullish — NDX ≥ 30,000 with VXN < 19:* **ARMED.** NDX needs **+3.64%**; VXN needs **−15.33%**.
  - *Bullish — Brent back below $92:* **ARMED and much closer — the largest single-trigger move of this series.** Needs **−7.48%** from $99.44, against −14.18% yesterday.
  - *Bullish — early US–China tariff-reduction announcement:* **ADVANCED again, still not concluded.** **China's Commerce Ministry says negotiators are striving to implement reciprocal tariff reductions on $30 billion of goods "at an early date"; Bessent meets He Lifeng this weekend; the summit is Sep 24 in Washington with a state dinner; the existing truce expires Nov 10** ([Daily Sabah](https://www.dailysabah.com/business/economy/china-us-eye-tariff-cuts-as-trump-xi-summit-nears), [Transport Topics](https://www.ttnews.com/articles/china-us-tariffs-energy)). **Barclays cautions the scope for a broad deal is limited and targeted reductions are more likely.**
  - *Neutralizer — FOMC 2026-09-16:* **RESOLVED. Hawkish.**
- **Notable lens flips: two, both upgrades, both energy-driven.** **Cross-asset −2 → −1 and Geopolitical −2 → −1.** Macro and Breadth remain pinned at the floor.

**Wednesday 2026-09-16 was a hawkish-Fed session, and the way the damage was distributed is the most important thing in this table.** **The Dow fell 1.21% — 631 points — while the NDX rose 0.02% and the Nasdaq Composite was flat at −0.01%** ([TheStreet](https://www.thestreet.com/stock-market-today/stock-market-today-dow-jones-sp-500-nasdaq-updates-sept-16-2026), [Motley Fool](https://www.fool.com/coverage/stock-market-today/2026/09/16/stock-market-today-sept-16-stocks-slip-as-fed-raises-rates/)). **That is a 1.23-percentage-point spread between the Dow and the Nasdaq-100 on a single session.** **AI and mega-cap tech absorbed a rate hike and a hawkish dot plot without falling — Dell, Intel and Nvidia all closed green on value buying — while the broad industrial and financial tape took the hit.** **For a 3× Nasdaq instrument this is the favourable side of a bad session. It is also, precisely, what narrow leadership looks like.**

**The bond market did what the dots told it to.** **The 10-year closed above 5% for the first time in this series and the 2s10s spread FLATTENED 6bp to +0.27%, reversing yesterday's steepening.** **The front end rose faster than the long end, which is the bond market pricing more hikes rather than more inflation — a different message from the one the long end was sending all last week.**

**This morning, Thursday 2026-09-17, futures are HIGHER: Dow futures +0.2%, S&P 500 futures +0.3%, Nasdaq-100 futures +0.5%, with Bloomberg attributing the recovery to Warsh's resolve on inflation reassuring markets** ([Bloomberg](https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2026-09-16/stock-market-today-dow-s-p-live-updates), [TradingEconomics](https://tradingeconomics.com/united-states/stock-market/news/535743)). **These are premarket quotes and no trigger in this report is evaluated on them.**

## Regime Stage Tracker
- **Current Stage:** **3 — Neutral / choppy**, and for the first time in three reads the classification does not hang on a single ambiguous number. **VIX is inside the 15–22 band on BOTH available measures — 15.99 on this morning's quote and 17.71 on the 09-16 settle — and VXN 22.44 is also inside.** **No Stage-4 threshold has fired: VIX needs +12.93% even from the settle, VXN needs +11.41%, NDX needs −1.88%, HY OAS needs +49bp.** **A Stage-2 case now technically exists — VIX 15.99 falls inside the Stage-2 band of 12–18 as well — but Stage 2 is defined as "mild bullish/grind", and a read with five bearish lenses, no bullish lens, and 30.6% of stocks above their 50-day average is not a bullish grind.** **Between Stage 2 and Stage 3 I take the lower: Stage 3.**
- **Stage Anchor:** **RE-ANCHORED to 2026-09-16 — the FOMC's first rate increase since 2023, 25bp to 3.75%–4.00% on a 12–0 vote, with a dot plot showing 16 of 18 participants expecting more this year.** **The previous anchor (2026-08-28, Chair Warsh's Jackson Hole keynote, which moved September hike odds from ~30% to a majority) has now resolved into the event it was anticipating. The regime is no longer "waiting for a hike"; it is "in a hiking cycle."** The **US–Iran conflict** (from 2026-02-28) continues to amplify through the energy channel, though that channel narrowed today.
- **Position:** **Week 1 of the confirmed-tightening leg.** Stage-3 range confirmed across sixteen consecutive reads (08-28 through 09-17).
- **Confidence:** **High.** Five lenses bearish (Macro −2, Breadth −2, Dealer flow −1, Cross-asset −1, Geopolitical −1), none bullish, two neutral. **No degradation cap: WebSearch was available, the option chain fetched, and the FOMC outcome, oil, breadth, sentiment, rates and trade inputs were all verified today.**
- **Bullish trigger (→ Stage 2):** NDX ≥ **30,000** (+3.64%) **with** VXN below **19** (−15.33%); **or** Brent confirmed below **$92** (−7.48% — **the closest bullish trigger in the report**); **or** a concluded US–China tariff-reduction announcement at or before the 09-24 summit; **or** the 10-year closing back below **5.00%** for two consecutive sessions.
- **Bearish trigger (→ Stage 4):** VIX sustained above **20** (+12.93% from the 09-16 settle); **or** **VXN > 25** (+11.41%); **or** NDX < **28,400** (−1.88%); **or** **HY OAS through 3.25% with IG above 0.90%** (from 2.76% / 0.80%, both 09-15).

## Regime Verdict
A Stage-3 range that has just absorbed a hawkish first hike without breaking — the NDX finished flat while the Dow lost 631 points, oil is unwinding a supply shock, and volatility is being crushed — sitting on top of a tape where roughly seven stocks in ten are below their 50-day average and the 10-year has closed above 5% for the first time since 2007, at **High** confidence.

**Data note.** WebSearch was available and the option chain fetched, so this is a full read with no degradation cap. **Resolved since last read:** the FOMC (hawkish); Finding 11, the Saudi pipeline contradiction, now resolved toward restoration — **but the 09-15 CNBC claim that the line was already "back at full 7 mb/d capacity" was wrong in substance even though it was right in direction: today's reporting is that Saudi Arabia will restore roughly HALF capacity within days and full operation within SIX WEEKS, while offering ship-to-ship transfers off Oman's Sohar port to blunt the shortfall** ([CNBC, Sep 17](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/09/17/oil-prices-today-wti-brent-hormuz-iran-war.html), [CNBC, Sep 16](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/09/16/oil-prices-today-brent-wti-hormuz-iran-war.html)). **New and unresolved:** the Brent LEVEL (engine $99.44 vs a CNBC figure of $105.81 for Thursday, and a TradingEconomics WTI print of $102.13 that would put Brent below WTI — structurally abnormal). **Still stale:** HY OAS 2.76% and IG OAS 0.80% carry 2026-09-15 stamps, so they do NOT cover the FOMC session. **Never retrieved in any read:** AAII, CFTC COT, margin debt, ETF flows, Citi Economic Surprise, insider/buyback activity, Copper/Gold, transports, Bitcoin this run. **NAAIM remains paywalled since 2026-08-01.**

## Diverging Signals

**First, and it is the defining feature of this session: the Dow and the Nasdaq-100 disagreed by 1.23 percentage points on the same hawkish Fed.** **DJI −1.21% (−631 points), NDX +0.02%.** **AI and mega-cap tech absorbed a rate hike, a 12–0 vote and a dot plot promising more, and did not fall — Dell, Intel and Nvidia all finished green on value buying** ([TheStreet](https://www.thestreet.com/stock-market-today/stock-market-today-dow-jones-sp-500-nasdaq-updates-sept-16-2026)). **For a leveraged Nasdaq instrument this is the good side of a bad tape. It is also the exact structure that breadth at 30.6% describes: the index is being carried. A market where the index is flat and 70% of stocks are below their 50-day average is not a calm market; it is a concentrated one, and concentration is a feature until it is the problem.**

**Second: the volatility market is crushing while the breadth reading is collapsing, and both are true.** **VIX 15.99 this morning (−9.71%), MOVE −3.56% to 80.73, term structure in contango at 0.898, IV/HV at a series-high 1.62.** **Against 30.6% of stocks above their 50-day average and a CNN Fear & Greed of 29.** **The options market has priced the event as done. The tape has not repaired anything. The honest reading is that the vol crush is about the calendar — a binary resolved — and not about the underlying condition, and a binary resolving is not the same as a risk going away.**

**Third, and this is a measurement trap worth stating plainly: the seller's cushion hit a series high for the wrong reason.** **IV/HV rose from 1.49 to 1.62, but BOTH inputs fell — quoted ATM IV 58.0% → 57.0%, realized HV20 38.8% → 35.0%.** **The ratio improved because realized volatility collapsed faster than implied did. That realized number is measured over the twenty quiet sessions leading INTO the FOMC — a window that ended yesterday, with quad-witching tomorrow.** **A ratio can look its best right before its denominator stops being representative. The 1.62 is arithmetically correct and I am not discounting it, but it is a backward-looking comparison being used to describe a forward-looking week.**

**Fourth: oil fell 6% and the 10-year still closed above 5%.** **If energy were the inflation driver the bond market was responding to, a −6.04% Brent session should have shown up in the long end. It did not — the 10-year rose and the curve FLATTENED 6bp, with the front end leading.** **That says the yield story is about the Fed path and about issuance, not about oil. The corollary matters for this instrument: the oil relief is real and it upgraded two lenses, but it does NOT relieve the discount-rate pressure on the NDX. Those turned out to be separate mechanisms after all.**
